summary: Oxmiq Labs is an early-stage deep-tech startup developing AI-driven materials discovery for sustainable chemistry. The team has strong academic credentials (PhDs from MIT/Stanford in computational chemistry and ML) but lacks commercial execution experience. Product is a proprietary generative model for inverse molecular design, currently in closed beta with 3 pilot partners. Market opportunity in green chemicals is large ($1T+ TAM) but sales cycles are long (18-24 months) and incumbents (Schrödinger, Citrine) have entrenched data moats. Traction is pre-revenue with $200K in non-dilutive grants and LOIs from two specialty chemical firms. Score of 50 reflects high technical promise offset by go-to-market uncertainty and thin defensibility beyond model weights.
rationale: Team (12/20): Founding trio has exceptional research pedigree (Nature/ Science publications) but zero prior startup or B2B sales experience; no commercial advisor on board. Defensibility (8/20): Core IP is model architecture + training pipeline; no patented composition-of-matter claims, and training data relies on public datasets (PubChem, Materials Project) accessible to competitors. Product (10/20): Generative model shows promising validation metrics (85% synthesis success rate in silico) but lacks wet-lab integration and regulatory/compliance tooling needed for enterprise adoption. Market & Why-Now (12/20): Tailwinds from IRA green chemistry incentives and supply-chain decarbonization mandates create urgency, but buyers are risk-averse R&D directors requiring extensive validation. Traction/Freshness (8/20): Pre-revenue with 3 design partners (no paid contracts), $200K SBIR grants, and 2 LOIs contingent on technical milestones; last meaningful product update 4 months ago. Critical risk: inability to convert pilots to paid contracts within 12 months given long sales cycles and limited runway ($600K remaining).
changeMyMind: Signs first paid pilot ($50K+) with a top-10 specialty chemical company with defined success criteria and timeline
